problem_type: The shared pointer renderer reintroduced a card-level waiting label inside a paid-card pointer, duplicating the question the card already asks.
symptom: The design-lab spend-single and spend-single-en states rendered the visible 「等你确认」 / Waiting for you label inside the pointer, while the SpendCardQ1 card title already asks for confirmation.
direct_cause: NodePointer's production-face status branch rendered awaiting_confirmation whenever density was card, even though the D2 card contract only allows queued and not-generated pointer status chips.
class_root: The shared pointer status boundary did not distinguish card-level decision state from per-shot execution state, so a new card surface could repeat the parent card's waiting copy.
affected_population: Paid-card single-pointer and any future card surface using NodePointer density=card while a shot is awaiting confirmation
Chinese and English SpendCardQ1 design-lab states
entry_points: NodePointer production-face status rendering for card density

invariant_owner_layer.why: NodePointer is the shared status renderer for card, row, and chip consumers; the focused test mounts a production awaiting-confirmation card and asserts that no status chip is emitted.

internal_only_reason: The distinction between a parent paid-card decision and per-shot execution status is an internal Nomi design contract.
invariants: A NodePointer card never repeats awaiting_confirmation; the parent card owns that question.
Card pointers may still show per-shot queued and not_generated status, while group and single-card consumers share the same rule.

door_reduction.why_not: The four readers are separate legitimate hosts: the production NodePointer implementation, its spend-card body consumer, and the independent NodePointer design-lab host and state fixtures. They must remain separate to exercise the shared component at each surface.

generality_proof: The status rule is enforced inside the shared NodePointer production-face renderer, so every current card consumer receives the same no-duplicate behavior regardless of whether it is the real spend card or a design-lab host. The focused component test covers the reported awaiting state; the existing design-lab spend-card walk covers Chinese and English single and grouped cards plus queued and not-generated states.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the shared production-face state consumed by NodePointer; card hosts use an explicit presentation flag to omit the parent-card awaiting-confirmation label.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Its NodePointerGroup now inherits the shared no-duplicate rule; the design-lab spend-single states exercise this consumer.
It imports the same production NodePointer component and remains covered by the NodePointer lab walk.
The awaiting_confirmation branch was removed from the one shared status condition; queued and not_generated branches remain explicit.

recurrence.reason: Any future card or pointer state can accidentally surface a parent-level decision label inside a child pointer unless the shared renderer owns the distinction and tests the card density boundary.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs NodePointer — four current reader doors converge on the shared NodePointer implementation.

rg -n 'awaiting_confirmation|productionShotCornerText|data-node-pointer-status' src/workbench/ai/pointer src/workbench/ai/v4 src/devlab/designLab/spendCard — checked all status-label producers and paid-card consumers.
design-lab-spend-card.walk.mjs — reported the visible duplicate in both zh and en single-card states and still asserts queued / not-generated labels separately.

prevention.invariant: PointerFaceArt emits only per-shot execution status chips for card density; awaiting_confirmation remains card-owned and is omitted.
prevention.failure_mode: A future awaiting-confirmation card render fails the focused NodePointer test and the design-lab spend-card walk before it can ship a duplicate label.
prevention.strategy: Delete the card-density awaiting branch from the shared renderer and retain the explicit queued/not-generated branches, with a focused component regression and bilingual lab coverage.

legacy_paths.rationale: The obsolete card-density awaiting_confirmation branch is removed from the existing shared renderer; the file remains as the owner.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: This is an internal presentation-state boundary with no dependency-controlled behavior.

migration: No persisted state changes; awaiting_confirmation remains in the production state model and is simply no longer rendered as a duplicate card pointer chip.
residual_risks: The full design-lab spend-card and NodePointer lanes still need a clean rerun after this source change.
ARIA labels continue to describe the pointer's state for accessibility; the visible duplicate chip is removed by design.
